source_review.notes: Reviewed PostgreSQL 18 materialized-view/refresh documentation, author-affiliated incremental-maintenance papers, Debezium 3.6 documentation, and Microsoft CQRS/materialized-view guidance against the cited claims. All seven final destinations returned HTTP 200. Product mechanisms are separated from end-to-end guarantees.

evidence: Checked S_k, P_v, M_{v,k}, projection equivalence, lag, drift, watermark, amplification, and idempotency terminology.
Checked source position, event time, commit order, and processing time remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Every equivalence or drift comparison names a common source position and projection version.

evidence: Recomputed two initial order-card rows from two customers and two orders.
Recomputed version-2 rename on order 10 and rejection of its duplicate.
Recomputed exactly one drift key after the missed version-3 rename and zero after rebuild.
Confirmed source and read-model cardinality both equal two.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Exact integer fixture values avoid rounding and aggregation ambiguity.

evidence: Re-derived exact correctness as M_{v,k}=P_v(S_k).
Re-derived incremental/full equivalence at a shared snapshot and source position.
Re-derived why maximum observed offset does not establish contiguous completeness.
Re-derived idempotence from rejection of versions not greater than current.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Asynchronous correctness remains conditional on the declared lag, ordering, gap, and delete contract.

evidence: Reviewed duplicate, stale, reordered, missing, poison, and retained-too-briefly changes.
Reviewed deletes, corrections, aggregate retractions, key changes, snapshot/stream handoff, and partial rebuild publication.
Reviewed schema versions, source failover, partition watermarks, privacy erasure, authorization, and consumer retirement.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable fixture covers duplicate/stale/missed changes only; broader cases are design-review obligations.

evidence: Rebuild derives one row per order key from authoritative customer/order dictionaries.
Incremental customer application accepts only a strictly greater version and updates every affected order card.
Drift compares union of expected and materialized keys plus exact values.
The verifier matched exact eight-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
invariant_checking.notes: Rebuild and incremental paths share the card shape, an independence limitation explicitly disclosed.

evidence: Reviewed the projection equivalence obligation at fixed version/watermark.
Reviewed idempotency, per-key ordering, contiguous completeness, and retraction obligations separately.
Reviewed versioned backfill/catch-up/reconcile/cutover/rollback sequence against atomic publication.
proof_review.notes: No proof is claimed for a broker, CDC connector, sink, or distributed end-to-end exactly-once path.

evidence: Separated historical snapshots, current derivations, aggregates, caches, and independent facts.
Separated mechanism claims for transactions/CDC/events/materialized views from freshness and correctness guarantees.
Separated bounded executable evidence from concurrency, crash, schema, broker, and production claims.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No latency or cost improvement is claimed without workload measurement.

evidence: The standard-library projection/rebuild model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
All seven final source destinations returned HTTP 200 on 2026-08-30.
Structure, links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and exact snippet expectations passed draft validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No database refresh, CDC stream, event broker, cache, migration, benchmark, restore, or production read model was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter treats denormalization as a versioned projection system with explicit authority, grain, maintenance, consistency, reconciliation, economics, and retirement.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed direct-query alternatives, transactional/CDC/event/cache routes, offsets, duplicates, gaps, deletes, freshness SLOs, rebuilds, cutovers, schema versions, privacy, cost, and rollback.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, projection model, ten distinct operational examples, and five exercises progress from classification through delivery algebra to zero-downtime replacement.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model do not certify a production materialized view, CDC/event pipeline, cache, snapshot handoff, delete/retraction path, schema migration, privacy workflow, benchmark, distributed consistency guarantee, or deployment fitness.
